verses.text: The LORD was kind to Sarah, just as he had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what he had promised.
Sarah became pregnant and gave Abraham a son in his old age, at the very time God had promised him.
Abraham named the son Sarah had given him Isaac.
When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, just as God had commanded him.
Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
Sarah said, "God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me."
She also said, "Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have given him a son in his old age."
The child grew up and was weaned from his mother's milk. On the day Isaac was weaned, Abraham held a great feast.
But Sarah saw that the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had given Abraham was making fun of Isaac.
So she said to Abraham, "Get rid of that slave woman and her son. That woman's son will never share the family inheritance with my son Isaac."
This upset Abraham very much, because Ishmael was his son too.
But God said to him, "Do not be upset about the boy and your slave woman. Listen to whatever Sarah tells you, because your family line will be counted through Isaac.
I will also make the son of the slave woman into a nation, because he is your child too."

Early the next morning Abraham took some food and a skin bag of water and gave them to Hagar. He put them on her shoulders and sent her away with the boy. She went on her way and wandered in the desert of Beersheba.
When the water in the skin was gone, she put the boy under one of the bushes.
Then she went and sat down about a bowshot away, because she thought, "I cannot watch the boy die." As she sat there, she began to cry loudly.
God heard the boy crying, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven. He said to her, "What is the matter, Hagar? Do not be afraid. God has heard the boy crying as he lies there.
Get up, lift the boy up and take him by the hand, because I will make him into a great nation."
Then God opened Hagar's eyes, and she saw a well of water. So she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.
God was with the boy as he grew up. He lived in the desert and became a skilled archer.
While he was living in the desert of Paran, his mother found a wife for him from Egypt.
At that time Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, said to Abraham, "God is with you in everything you do.
So now promise me here in front of God that you will not trick me or my children or my descendants. Show me and the land where you are living the same kindness that I have shown you."
Abraham said, "I promise."
Then Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well of water that Abimelech's servants had taken by force.
But Abimelech said, "I do not know who has done this. You did not tell me, and I heard about it only today."
So Abraham brought sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two men made an agreement.
Abraham set apart seven female lambs from the flock.
Abimelech asked Abraham, "What is the meaning of these seven female lambs you have set apart?"
Abraham replied, "Accept these seven lambs from me as proof that I dug this well."
So that place was called Beersheba, which means "well of the oath", because the two men made a promise there.
After they had made the agreement at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army went back to the land of the Philistines.
Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called on the name of the LORD, the God who lives for ever.
And Abraham stayed in the land of the Philistines for a long time.
